motion.title: Natural Walk Cycle
motion.text: Show one adult subject walking at a believable everyday pace with natural weight transfer, arm swing, foot contact, fabric movement, and gaze. Keep the route and destination clear, preserve product visibility, and avoid looping steps, sliding feet, altered limbs, or clothing that changes between frames.

motion.title: Controlled Product Turn
motion.text: Rotate [product] slowly and steadily through a partial turn so its form, finish, scale, and key features become clear. Keep the axis stable, speed consistent, and light behavior physically plausible across every surface. End on a readable hero angle without warping logos, shifting seams, or changing material color.

motion.title: Hand-Led Reveal
motion.text: Use one calm, anatomically natural hand action to reveal, open, lift, unfold, or place [product]. Begin with a clear before state, execute the gesture at a deliberate pace, and finish on the important feature. Keep fingers distinct, grip credible, and the product unobstructed at the reveal moment.

motion.title: Fabric Breath
motion.text: Create subtle, believable fabric motion from a small body shift, a light breeze, or a gentle touch. Let the material's weight, drape, fold, and recovery match its apparent construction. Keep the movement minimal enough to preserve product detail; avoid rubbery cloth, extreme fluttering, or texture flicker.

motion.title: Single Ritual Action
motion.text: Show one complete, everyday ritual action involving [product], such as preparing, applying, packing, pouring, arranging, or pausing. Use a clear beginning, middle, and end with purposeful hand placement and an unhurried rhythm. Keep the environment stable and eliminate extra gestures that dilute the story.

motion.title: Micro-Expression Beat
motion.text: Hold a close portrait while the subject makes one restrained, natural emotional shift—an attentive glance, a small exhale, a soft smile, or a thoughtful change in focus. Preserve facial identity, eye alignment, skin texture, and lighting. The movement should feel observed, not acted or looped.

motion.title: Step-by-Step Assembly
motion.text: Show [product or object] being assembled, adjusted, or prepared through one clearly legible step. Use correct sequence, realistic tool contact, and a stable work surface. The action should reveal practical value and end on a completed, functional state without skipping, morphing parts, or hiding important details.

motion.title: Environmental Life
motion.text: Keep the camera and primary subject mostly still while adding subtle environmental life: shifting tree shadows, soft steam, a curtain moving, rain on glass, distant pedestrian motion, or dust in light. Use only motion that suits the location and maintains the scene's realism; it should deepen atmosphere without competing with the message.

motion.title: Physical Before / After
motion.text: Show a concrete transformation from a clear before state to a clear after state through one continuous, believable action or reveal. Match camera position, product identity, lighting, and scale so the difference is understandable. Make the change honest and specific rather than relying on a magical unexplained morph.

motion.title: Pause, Notice, Continue
motion.text: Create a short human story beat: the subject moves naturally, pauses to notice or engage with [product], then continues with a changed but subtle sense of purpose. Keep the gesture small, timing realistic, and the visual arc understandable without dialogue. Preserve consistent identity, wardrobe, and environment throughout.

videoMoves.title: Static Tableau
videoMoves.text: Lock the camera in a carefully composed static frame and let the subject or environment provide the movement. Hold long enough for the key action and detail to register, with stable geometry, exposure, and focus. Use this when stillness makes the composition more powerful than camera motion.

videoMoves.title: Slow Motivated Push-In
videoMoves.text: Make one slow, smooth push-in from a contextual wider frame toward the face, product, or action detail that carries the emotional payoff. Keep the camera path straight and focus stable, then settle on a readable final composition. Do not accelerate abruptly or turn the move into a zoom effect.

videoMoves.title: Gentle Pullback Reveal
videoMoves.text: Begin close on [product or detail], then pull back gradually to reveal the larger context, location, or human use case. Maintain a stable focal relationship and let the newly revealed information explain the detail. End with enough time for viewers to understand the full scene.

videoMoves.title: Lateral Tracking Move
videoMoves.text: Track smoothly alongside a moving or stationary subject at a consistent distance and height. Use foreground and background parallax to add depth while keeping the face or product readable. Match the speed to the subject's action and avoid jitter, elastic backgrounds, or unmotivated reframing.

videoMoves.title: Small Product Orbit
videoMoves.text: Move in a restrained arc around [product] to reveal form, depth, and material response to light. Keep the product fixed in space, the horizon stable, and the orbit slow enough to inspect details. Avoid a full dizzying spin, shifting product features, or reflections that do not track with the movement.

videoMoves.title: Vertical Tilt Reveal
videoMoves.text: Use a single smooth upward or downward tilt to reveal [product, subject, or environmental feature] from a meaningful starting detail. Keep the motion controlled and end on a composition that explains the relationship between the two visual elements. Avoid a whip-like speed or unstable vertical lines.

videoMoves.title: Top-Down Glide
videoMoves.text: Move slowly across an overhead arrangement of [product, tools, or ingredients], maintaining perpendicular camera angle, consistent scale, and soft even light. Use the glide to reveal a sequence, comparison, or system. Keep objects aligned and prevent them from drifting, duplicating, or changing orientation.

videoMoves.title: Restrained Handheld Observer
videoMoves.text: Use lightly handheld camera movement that feels like a present human observer: subtle breathing, gentle reframing, and controlled natural imperfection. Keep the frame readable, the horizon reasonably stable, and the subject in focus. Do not use excessive shake, sudden lurches, or digital jitter that distracts from the story.

videoMoves.title: Purposeful Rack Focus
videoMoves.text: Hold the camera still and shift focus deliberately from [foreground subject or product] to [background subject or detail], or reverse. Make the focus transition smooth, timed to the narrative handoff, and end with the new focal element clearly sharp. Preserve physical depth and avoid focus hunting or artificial edge halos.

videoMoves.title: Doorway Pass-Through
videoMoves.text: Move smoothly through a doorway, arch, curtain, or other environmental threshold to carry the viewer from one spatial context to the next. Keep the path physically plausible, exposure adapting naturally, and the new scene immediately readable. Use the threshold as a story transition, not as a random visual effect.

platformPresets.title: Social Vertical Story
platformPresets.text: Design for a vertical social video with the subject, product, and key action large enough for a phone screen. Keep important faces, logos, and any concise copy away from top and bottom interface areas, leaving comfortable safe margins. Establish the hook immediately, use one clear visual idea, and retain high contrast for mobile viewing.

platformPresets.title: Square Feed Clarity
platformPresets.text: Compose a square social feed asset with one centered or deliberately offset focal subject, balanced negative space, and a readable product silhouette. Keep critical detail within a conservative central area for cross-platform cropping. Use concise graphic elements only when they improve the message; prioritize immediate visual recognition.

platformPresets.title: Landscape Story Frame
platformPresets.text: Design a widescreen landscape frame that uses horizontal space to establish environment, movement direction, and cinematic depth. Keep faces and products large enough to read while using left-right space for story context rather than empty decoration. Protect key information from edge crops and maintain a stable horizon.

platformPresets.title: Carousel Sequence System
platformPresets.text: Create a cohesive multi-frame carousel system: frame 1 delivers the hook, middle frames reveal one clear point or step at a time, and the final frame lands on the takeaway or action. Maintain the same palette, type hierarchy, subject identity, and product fidelity throughout. Each frame must be independently legible and visually connected to the next.

platformPresets.title: Thumbnail-First Cover
platformPresets.text: Compose the opening or cover frame to work as a small thumbnail: a single large face, product, or visual contrast; clear silhouette; concise optional headline; and no fine detail essential to understanding. Leave safe room around the focal point for platform overlays and make the first frame truthful to the content that follows.

platformPresets.title: Product Demo Delivery
platformPresets.text: Structure a product-demo delivery around one task: establish the product, show the key action from a readable angle, reveal the result, and end on the product or next step. Use stable framing, clean sound-ready visual pacing, accurate details, and minimal text. Do not sacrifice clarity for fast cuts or decorative transitions.

platformPresets.title: Testimonial Proof Format
platformPresets.text: Create a testimonial-ready format with a direct, well-lit person, a clear product relationship, and room for a short verified quote or caption. Use an honest conversational setting and keep visual claims specific and supportable. Maintain safe space for text, clean audio framing, and consistent visual identity across testimonial variations.

platformPresets.title: Seamless Loop
platformPresets.text: Design a short looping asset where the final frame naturally reconnects to the first through matched position, light, camera, and action. Use a small repeatable gesture or visual rhythm, keep the loop unobtrusive, and ensure the product remains consistent. Avoid obvious jump resets, reversed motion, or loop mechanics that distract from the message.

platformPresets.title: Caption-Safe Interview
platformPresets.text: Frame an interview or speaking subject with comfortable headroom, eye line, and a clean background, leaving a clear lower-third and caption-safe zone without covering the face, hands, or product. Keep visual rhythm gentle enough for reading. Use uncluttered styling, stable camera, and expressive but natural gestures.

platformPresets.title: Cross-Platform Master
platformPresets.text: Build a flexible master composition with the essential subject, product, and message contained within a central safe area that can crop cleanly to vertical, square, and landscape versions. Keep secondary environmental detail toward the edges, avoid essential text at boundaries, and maintain a strong core image across all output adaptations.

editingTransitions.title: Purposeful Straight Cut
editingTransitions.text: Use a clean straight cut when the next shot adds new information, changes viewpoint, or advances action. Match screen direction, lighting, and story logic so the edit feels intentional. Favor this direct cut over a decorative transition when clarity and pacing matter most.

editingTransitions.title: Cut on Action
editingTransitions.text: Cut during a continuous physical action—reach, turn, open, place, walk, or look—so the movement carries the viewer smoothly into the next angle. Match the action's timing, direction, object position, and subject identity across the cut. Use it to hide the edit while making the sequence feel more energetic.

editingTransitions.title: Visual Match Cut
editingTransitions.text: Transition between two shots by matching a shared shape, color, motion, object position, or gesture. Let the visual resemblance create a meaningful connection between ideas, locations, or moments. Keep the match simple and legible; do not force unrelated imagery into a confusing visual trick.

editingTransitions.title: J-Cut Audio Lead
editingTransitions.text: Let the sound, voice, or relevant environment from the next scene begin slightly before the picture changes, then cut to the matching visual. Use the audio lead to create anticipation or smooth a location change. Keep the sound motivated by the scene and avoid abrupt, unexplained audio overlaps.

editingTransitions.title: L-Cut Emotional Hold
editingTransitions.text: Allow the sound from the current shot to continue briefly after cutting to the next image. Use the overlap to hold an emotion, explain a reaction, or connect a detail shot to the prior moment. Keep timing natural and ensure the continuing audio still makes sense over the new visual.

editingTransitions.title: Restrained Cross Dissolve
editingTransitions.text: Use a short, restrained cross dissolve only to signal soft passage of time, memory, reflection, or a gentle change in place. Choose shots with compatible light, composition, and motion so the blend remains readable. Avoid repeated dissolves that soften pace or create an unintended slideshow effect.

editingTransitions.title: Motivated Whip-Pan Bridge
editingTransitions.text: Use a brief, motivated whip-pan movement as a bridge between two similarly directed shots when the story calls for energy or a playful change of place. Match motion direction, speed, exposure, and landing composition. Keep the blur controlled and use it sparingly so it feels like camera language, not a generic effect.

editingTransitions.title: In-Camera Object Wipe
editingTransitions.text: Let a real object, hand, door, fabric, or foreground surface pass across the lens to conceal a cut, then reveal the next scene. Match the direction and timing of the wipe and keep the object relevant to the action. The transition should feel physically captured, not like an unrelated digital overlay.

editingTransitions.title: Rhythmic Detail Montage
editingTransitions.text: Build a short sequence of varied detail, medium, and context shots around one product or action, cutting to a clear visual rhythm. Each shot must add a distinct piece of information—texture, use, reaction, scale, or outcome. Maintain a consistent palette and direction; avoid repetition that adds no story value.

editingTransitions.title: Hold for the Payoff
editingTransitions.text: After the key reveal, reaction, or product result, hold the final frame long enough for the viewer to process it before cutting away. Keep the composition stable, product legible, and visual information uncluttered. Use this pause as a deliberate ending beat rather than letting the sequence stop abruptly.

aspectOutput.title: Vertical 9:16 Mobile
aspectOutput.text: Deliver in a 9:16 vertical composition optimized for phone viewing. Keep the subject large, the focal action centered within a conservative safe area, and essential text away from top and bottom interface zones. Use vertical depth, intentional headroom, and a clear first-second hook; avoid tiny subjects and edge-cropped details.

aspectOutput.title: Landscape 16:9 Master
aspectOutput.text: Deliver in a 16:9 landscape master with balanced horizontal storytelling, stable horizon, and room for environment without shrinking the product or subject. Keep essential action and any copy inside a safe central band so the edit can adapt to other formats. Preserve fine detail for high-resolution playback.

aspectOutput.title: Square 1:1 Feed
aspectOutput.text: Deliver in a 1:1 square composition with one immediately readable hero subject or product, controlled negative space, and balanced visual weight. Avoid relying on wide environmental information or tall vertical gestures that crop poorly. Keep all critical features and concise copy within the central square.

aspectOutput.title: Portrait 4:5 Feed
aspectOutput.text: Deliver in a 4:5 portrait composition optimized for feed visibility. Use the extra vertical space for a clear subject, product context, or concise stacked message while preserving comfortable top and bottom margins. Keep details large enough to inspect in a scrolling feed and avoid interface-sensitive edge placement.

aspectOutput.title: Cover & Thumbnail Frame
aspectOutput.text: Create a dedicated cover frame that remains clear at small size: one strong product, face, or visual contrast; high subject separation; and optional short, accurate headline. Avoid fine type, crowded object groups, and ambiguous gestures. The cover must truthfully represent the video while encouraging a viewer to start it.

aspectOutput.title: Caption-Safe Delivery
aspectOutput.text: Deliver a composition with deliberate clean space for captions, subtitles, or translated copy without covering faces, hands, product features, or key action. Keep background contrast sufficient for readable type and avoid fast visual changes behind the caption area. The story should remain understandable with sound off.

aspectOutput.title: Product Detail Crop
aspectOutput.text: Deliver a tight crop designed to make one product feature, material, or action inspectable. Keep the critical plane sharp, preserve correct color and proportions, and include just enough context to identify the item. Do not crop through essential construction or use blur, glare, or text to conceal the detail.

aspectOutput.title: Loop-Ready End Frame
aspectOutput.text: Deliver an end frame that can reconnect visually to the opening frame: matched camera position, product placement, light, and a compatible subject gesture. Keep the final composition complete even when viewed alone. Avoid sudden end-frame changes that create a visible jump when the video loops.

aspectOutput.title: High-Resolution Clean Master
aspectOutput.text: Deliver a clean high-resolution master with stable detail, controlled gradients, accurate color, natural texture, and no compression artifacts, burnt-in platform UI, watermarks, or accidental text. Maintain consistent exposure and product fidelity across the full asset so it can be adapted, cropped, or encoded for multiple channels.

aspectOutput.title: Multi-Ratio Safe Composition
aspectOutput.text: Deliver a crop-flexible composition where the product, subject, and core action sit within a central safe zone suitable for vertical, square, and landscape versions. Place nonessential atmosphere at the edges, keep copy modular, and avoid camera moves that require the full wide frame to make sense.
